newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq 1996 European sales rise 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Compaq 1996 European sales rise 12 pct.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. said on Thursday its European sales rose 12 percent in 1996 to $6 billion, powered by a strong fourth quarter and solid gains in portable PC and server sales.
European gains were dampened by weaker results in Germany, where revenue rose 7.6 percent to 1.4 billion marks ($832.9 million) as unit sales stalled.
Kurt Dobitsch, head of Compaq's German unit, said he was "satisfied" with results in that country, although he admitted Compaq and other large PC makers saw "stagnating market share" in 1996.
"With growth of only one percent, the home market showed a flat and disappointing development curve," he told a news conference.
Market researcher Dataquest estimated Compaq unit sales fell 10 percent in Germany. Compaq was expected to announce a new German strategy on Thursday.
Compaq said unit sales of desktop PCs rose 27 percent across Europe, while portable unit sales increased 36 percent and servers 32 percent.
In the fourth quarter, revenue for Europe, the Middle East and Africa rose 44 percent, Compaq said.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.680 German Marks)
